title: Solid-state battery dendrite deflection
dek: A laboratory technique redirected a destructive failure instead of eliminating it. Replication and scale will decide whether that geometry travels beyond one cell architecture.

canonicalSubject.name: Biaxial dendrite deflection in solid electrolytes

trackingTerms: shape memory alloy ring battery dendrites
whyTracked: The mechanism is specific, consequential, and falsifiable, with clear tests in independent laboratories and commercially relevant cells.

current.assessment: The peer-reviewed laboratory result is real within its tested system, but manufacturability, pack-level safety, lifetime, and independent replication remain open.
current.nextReviewTrigger: Review for independent replication, larger-format cells, manufacturing integration, or end-to-end safety and lifetime measurements.

openQuestions: Will an independent group reproduce the deflection mechanism?
Can the applied stress be integrated into practical cell manufacturing and cycling conditions?
Does the strategy improve safety and lifetime at commercially relevant scale?

watchFor.trigger: Another research group tests dendrite deflection under biaxial stress.
A study reports practical architecture, scale, lifetime, and full-system tradeoffs.

observations.headline: Point-zero observation
observations.summary: Researchers reported that biaxial compression redirected lithium dendrites perpendicular to the electric field in a garnet solid electrolyte, allowing many internal dendrites to form without immediately short-circuiting the cell.

sources.title: Dendrite initiation and deflection in biaxially stressed solid electrolytes

observations.headline: Admitted to The Wake pilot
observations.summary: Admitted because it provides a clean laboratory baseline against which replication and practical scale-up can be compared.
